title: History of Science Museum Oxford / Royal Microscopical Society: cabinet survival, manuscript catalogues, and digital re-addressing
core_result: Oxford preserves an institutional-scale Royal Microscopical Society slide cabinet together with a hierarchical digital catalogue and a substantial RMS manuscript/archive ecology. This closes collection survival and modern re-addressing at S level, while the historical catalogue/event → specific surviving slide crosswalk remains open.

critical_guards: Do not assume that every Small Worlds catalogue record belongs to the single RMS cabinet. The database covers the Museum's broader microscopical-specimen collection.
Do not assume MSS Royal Microscopical Society nos. 5, 13 or 18 are catalogues of the surviving RMS cabinet until historical numbers, maker names, subjects, drawer order or labels are compared.
The modern container/drawer/slide/specimen hierarchy is a museum/database address system created by cataloguing. It should not be back-projected as the nineteenth-century RMS storage ontology.
Permanent-loan / deposited-on-loan / purchased-presented manuscript statuses belong to different collection layers and must remain distinct.
research_payoff: Oxford provides the institutional-scale counterpart to Cole. Cole shows a small publication-specific cabinet whose fixed numbers bind glass back to print. Oxford shows a large society cabinet that survived long enough to be translated into a modern nested database while related RMS manuscript catalogues and archival records remain available in the same museum. The next historical question is therefore not survival but crosswalk: which old catalogue address became which modern cabinet/database address?
next_bounded_actions: Take MSS Royal Microscopical Society 5 (Gwatkin molluscs), 13 (mainly diatoms, 1860-69), or 18 (Histological Catalogue, 1892) as a bounded historical list.
Extract two or three diagnostic entries containing maker/subject/number language.
Search the Small Worlds catalogue for exact maker/subject/label matches and compare container/drawer/slide coordinates.
Promote to item-level S only where an independent historical address and modern object identity converge; otherwise retain architecture-level S.
